title: Writing Your First jQuery Program
subtopics: Verifying the result in browser developer tools
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of writing your first jquery program in a jQuery application.
Apply selecting a heading in a small example and describe its expected result.
Verify changing text content with an explicit test or browser observation.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will work through writing your first jquery program with a focused jQuery example. The subtopics below preserve the supplied curriculum coverage and connect the API idea to a small browser interface.
content.why_it_matters: This topic is useful because it turns selecting a heading into a repeatable implementation choice. A page must load one compatible jQuery build before dependent application code runs. Keep the chosen version explicit and verify the loaded file in the browser Network and Console panels.

content_blocks.expected_output: After the page is ready, clicking #change-title updates the heading text and adds is-active. The page needs a matching button and heading.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Use a local HTML page with jQuery 4.0.0 loaded before app.js for JavaScript snippets. HTML and package-manager snippets can be checked as configuration examples. Run the interaction in browser DevTools, inspect the DOM/Network panel, and compare actual behavior with the expected result. Do not submit learner code to the production API for arbitrary execution.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the original markup and code, clear console/network filters, reload the local page, and repeat the same interaction. For a request example, return the mock endpoint to its original response before retrying.

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Start with a known DOM structure, apply the pattern for writing your first jquery program, and test one normal case plus one edge case. Keep selectors scoped to the intended component and verify the real browser result.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Set up a minimal local page for writing your first jquery program. Verify script order, the selected jQuery 4.0.0 build, and the console before adding more code.

task_acceptance_criteria: The implementation demonstrates writing your first jquery program using a current, documented approach.
The learner records the expected and actual behavior and checks at least one edge case.
The example preserves semantic HTML and does not render untrusted data as HTML.
The test setup and any runtime limitation are documented honestly.
hints: First identify which DOM nodes and runtime state are involved in writing your first jquery program.
Make one small change, inspect the resulting element or request, and compare it with the expected result.
If the result differs, check the selector, script order, browser console, event target, and relevant API documentation before adding more code.
content.expected_output: After the page is ready, clicking #change-title updates the heading text and adds is-active. The page needs a matching button and heading.
common_mistakes: Assuming a selector matched an element without checking the collection length.
Confusing jQuery collections with native DOM elements or live properties with markup attributes.
Using .html() with untrusted data or assuming client-side validation enforces server rules.
Treating a demo snippet as production-ready without testing failure and accessibility states.
